title: The dog at the shack
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The uncle and the dog. The uncle has had dogs. He looks at this one and says 'that one's a coast dog.' It's the first time anyone's agreed with Wood about anything.

panels.composition: The shack. The UNCLE in the door. BARNABY at his boots, sniffing. WOOD and GULLY.

image.prompt: an old man in a rain hood standing in a shack doorway with a small dog sniffing his boots, two young men watching, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle looking down. The dog looking up. Two flat faces.

image.prompt: an old weathered man and a small scruffy dog looking at each other, both expressionless, black and white, no words

balloons.text: That's what I said. The vet said hound.

image.prompt: an old man speaking flatly from a shack doorway, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog going into the shack ahead of everyone. The uncle letting him. Gully looking at Wood: that never happens.

image.prompt: a small dog walking into a bait shack ahead of an old man who lets him pass, a teenager exchanging a look with a young man, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Coast dog.' The uncle agrees with Wood, once. 'Vet's from Corvallis.'
